name: Cassava Brown Streak Disease
description: A viral disease affecting cassava roots, causing necrotic brown streaks in the tuberous roots. It is spread by whiteflies and infected cuttings.
symptoms: Yellow to brown chlorotic patches on leaves along veins
Necrotic brown streaks and corky tissue inside roots
Root rot and internal discoloration reducing marketability
Leaf symptoms may be subtle or absent while roots are affected
Reduced starch content in affected tubers
causes: Cassava brown streak virus transmitted by whiteflies
Movement of contaminated planting material between regions
treatments: No curative treatment for viral infection
Destroy severely infected plants and roots
Apply insecticides to reduce whitefly vector populations
prevention: Avoid moving planting material from affected areas
Early and frequent roguing of symptomatic plants
